artifacts.title: Williams v. Chesapeake Presbytery

matches.evidence: …ether he be guilty or not with respect to the Indictment of September 25, 2018 (BCO 32-3.3). V. REASONING Chesapeake Presbytery commissioned its PJC to investigate TE Willia…

Yes. The complaint is sustained and the action of Presbytery approving the PJC report is annulled, thereby returning the matter to the PJC. The PJC is free to dismiss the case, or to adjudicate the case with process according to the principles set forth herein

artifacts.synopsis: Chesapeake Presbytery's PJC attempted to convert a BCO 32 case of process into a BCO 38-1 case without process after TE Williams partially pled guilty, confusing the two distinct procedures. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled the Presbytery's action, finding the conflation of BCO 32 and 38-1 violated the due process rights of the accused.
